analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES Micron delivers; Oracle Tencent deal; Google Argon; ACN results in focus; IFX AI datacentre demand Scout24, DT, OMC 1 Oct 2026
key_insights: Micron reported a Q4 beat and a Q1 guide well above consensus. Management says AI and HBM demand outstrips supply, most 2027 HBM capacity is contracted at higher prices, and DRAM and NAND stay tight through 2027-28 despite rising capex. Shares were broadly flat after hours because expectations and valuation were already high.

Read-through from Micron favors memory suppliers (SK Hynix, Samsung) and wafer-fab equipment and test names (LCRX, AMAT, ASML, Tokyo Electron, Advantest). Japanese equipment and memory stocks led Asia this morning while Korean names were more subdued. The desk's main risks are higher capex, valuation and eventual scrutiny of AI customer returns, not near-term demand.

The desk says its IB discussion this morning debated favoring memory and select WFE over pure foundry/logic for the next few quarters of the cycle, and the author says it 'feels like it'. Jim is raising revenue estimates for the next 3 years by more than 14% per year and EPS by more than 12% per year.

Rising DRAM prices are a negative for memory-heavy hardware names. Ericsson was pushed lower on DRAM costs and on Jabil describing a subdued 5G market expected to stay muted near term, with no volume offset to the margin pressure.

The GS memory pricing tracker points to continued strength in 4Q26. TrendForce expects PC, server and mobile DRAM prices to rise 13-18%, 10-15% and 0-5% quarter on quarter, and NAND prices to rise 15-20%. The GS DRAM Sentiment Indicator stayed moderately positive in September on rising DDR5 and DDR4 pricing and record 130% y/y server ODM revenue growth.

Power semis are tightening like memory. Infineon's Taiwan MD cites rack power density heading to hundreds of kW to 1 MW, 800 V architectures and more SiC/GaN content, and sees supply normalizing only in 2-3 years. Taiwanese names are following Infineon and onsemi with non-contract price hikes of 10-15%, concentrated in MOSFETs.

FT/Reuters report Tencent signed a five-year, roughly $7bn lease of Oracle Asia capacity for about 100k advanced AI chips (press, not company-confirmed). It supports Oracle's capacity and backlog narrative alongside OpenAI and ByteDance, and the desk will watch how Oracle CDS reacts. It gives Tencent frontier compute without waiting for domestic silicon.

Google gave back some gains on reports of internal doubts over Gemini 4, then launched the flagship 'Argon' model after the close. Google claims strong coding performance, but some benchmarks and employee feedback look less convincing and hands-on access is limited. The real test is developer use in practice.

Accenture reports later today. Focus is bookings and book-to-bill, whether AI work is converting to durable revenue, US federal demand stabilization and initial FY2027 guidance. GIR expects FY2027 constant-currency growth of 3-4%, made of 50-150bp organic, about 100bp from lapping federal headwinds and 150-200bp from M&A.

The IT-services backdrop is subdued as clients redirect spending and use AI to cut costs. GIR's Indian IT preview forecasts organic growth of 1.8% in FY2027 and 3.2% in FY2028 with flat margins and broad estimate cuts, and downgrades LTM to Sell.

Scout24 was added to the GS Conviction List. Adam is in line with consensus on Professional revenue but ahead on Private, where new products such as deposit guarantees drive subscriber growth. He is also above consensus on margin by FY28E and on buybacks of EUR350m in 2026 and EUR250m in 2027. The Q3 delivery is the catalyst.

Omnicom preview: GIR expects Q3 organic core growth of 4.9% (reported 20 October) and adjusted EPS of $2.76 against $2.65 consensus. Recent account wins largely offset the $1.1bn Pepsi media loss. At 6x 2027 EPS versus WPP at 7x, the valuation leaves room for a positive reaction.

Samsung: GIR cut its 3Q26 operating-profit estimate by 5% to W106tn on a stronger won, still above W100tn and in line with consensus. 2027-28 forecasts stay 8-17% above the Street on HBM-led DRAM pricing, and next year's HBM revenue is expected to exceed W100tn.

Synopsys Investor Day: GIR was favorably impressed. Long-term targets are about 15% revenue CAGR FY26-30, 50% operating margin in FY30 and mid-20% EPS growth to $35.00 in FY30, all above the Street. Themes are AI monetization (including an OpenAI partnership) and a Design IP roadmap for hyperscalers. The stock is up about 5%.

US trading color: Q3 ended with a large $11.5B MOC sell imbalance for month end. Activity was spotty at a 4 out of 10 on the desk's scale. Yields rose as the street looked through a softer PCE. Short-interest and non-profitable tech pockets outperformed in an unwind-style tape, with a Software over Semis tilt ahead of MU earnings.

Rates: after the softer PCE and comments from Fed President Williams, GIR pushed its Fed hike timing from October to December and sees an October hike as unlikely. It now expects 3.0% core PCE growth on a Q4/Q4 basis, well below the median FOMC participant forecast of 3.4%, which the desk says should help stabilize equities into Q4.

Telecom items: Handelsblatt alleges Deutsche Telekom and SoftBank disadvantaged T-Mobile minority shareholders in the 2020 Sprint merger, with potential damages of up to $10.1bn, and DT has not commented. EU states are pushing for flexible, case-by-case timelines instead of a 36-month deadline for removing Huawei and ZTE gear, which is read as capex relief.

Other AI items: DeepSeek is partnering with Huawei on open-source tools for Ascend chips, ElevenLabs completed a $300m tender at a $22bn valuation, and the US launched America.gov as an AI front door to government. A commentary on AI assistants versus marketplaces asks whether agents take high-margin discovery economics from incumbents.

Amadeus read-through: IATA August global RPKs fell 0.8% y/y with load factor down 0.9pp to 85.1%. YTD RPK growth of 0.4% is tracking below IATA's +2.1% FY26 outlook, mainly on Middle East and APAC softness.

earnings_insights: Micron Q4 (reported): revenue $54.23bn and adjusted EPS $33.42, both ahead of expectations. Q1 guidance (company guide): revenue $61.5bn and EPS of about $38.15, well above consensus. Shares were broadly flat after hours.
Accenture (reports later today, so all figures are estimates): consensus Q4 revenue around $18bn and EPS $3.18-3.19. GIR forecasts FY2027 constant-currency growth of 3-4% (GIR estimate).

Omnicom Q3 (reports 20 October, GIR estimates): organic core revenue growth 4.9%, reported revenue $6.17bn, adjusted EBIT $1.14bn and adjusted EPS $2.76 versus consensus of $2.65. Media growth about 10%, advertising down 8%, healthcare flat, PR up 7%, experiential up 5%.

Samsung 3Q26 (GIR estimate): operating profit cut 5% to W106tn on a stronger won, broadly in line with consensus. 2027-28 estimates are 8-17% above the Street and 2027 HBM revenue is expected above W100tn.
Jabil fell about 10% on a beat/raise (reported), weighing on sentiment into Micron's print. FactSet rose about 4% on a mixed print and outlook (reported).
Ericsson was pushed lower on rising DRAM prices and Jabil describing a subdued 5G market expected to stay muted near term.
GIR Indian IT Services preview (GIR estimate): organic growth of 1.8% in FY2027 and 3.2% in FY2028, flat margins, broad estimate cuts.

Scout24 (GIR estimate vs VA consensus): average private subscribers 616k in 2027 vs 589k and 700k in 2028 vs 651k, margin of about 64% by FY28E vs 63.4%, buybacks of EUR350m in 2026 and EUR250m in 2027.
Synopsys Investor Day targets (company targets, above Street): about 15% revenue CAGR FY26-30, 50% operating margin in FY30 and mid-20% EPS growth to $35.00 in FY30.

Rising DRAM prices squeeze margins at memory-heavy hardware and telecom equipment makers, with no volume offset in a subdued 5G market.
US federal demand and AI-to-revenue conversion at IT-services firms, tested by Accenture results.
Spotty activity, intense focus on oil and rates, a midterm overhang and high-velocity narrative shifts within AI.
Yields continuing to rise and the possibility of a Fed hike (GIR now expects December).
Legal and reputational risk for Deutsche Telekom from the Handelsblatt allegations, with potential damages of up to $10.1bn.
Soft air passenger demand, with RPKs tracking below IATA's FY26 outlook.
Mixed early reception for Google's Argon model and limited hands-on access.
Advertising and commission profit pools could migrate to AI agents if agents do not generate incremental demand.
vol_and_positioning: Month-end MOC imbalance was $11.5B to sell. Pensions were modelled to sell $30.5b of US equities, which ranked in the 89th percentile over the past three years.
Desk saw an unwind-style tape with short-interest and non-profitable tech pockets outperforming, and a Software over Semis tilt on earnings reactions plus end-of-quarter and usual sector vol.

GS floor activity was 4 on a 1-10 scale, finishing +6% net to buy. Asset managers were net buyers (tech and macro) while hedge funds were roughly flat, with demand in healthcare versus supply in tech and industrials.
The desk notes the seasonality chart of the SOX makes Q4 look interesting.
geopolitical: EU member states are pushing to replace a proposed mandatory 36-month deadline for removing Huawei and ZTE equipment with a case-by-case timetable. Full replacement could cost up to EUR40bn and Deutsche Telekom and Vodafone still rely on Huawei in several markets.
DeepSeek is partnering with Huawei to open-source tools optimized for Ascend chips, strengthening China's domestic AI ecosystem and reducing reliance on Nvidia.
Tencent reportedly leased Oracle Asia capacity for about 100k advanced AI chips, getting frontier compute without waiting on domestic silicon.
IATA attributes softer air travel demand mainly to the Middle East and APAC.
The desk cites an intense focus on oil and rates and a looming midterm election overhang as part of a demanding macro backdrop.

tension_points.bull_case: AI and HBM demand outstrips supply, most 2027 HBM is contracted at higher prices and DRAM and NAND are expected to stay tight through 2027-28. Jim raised revenue estimates by more than 14% per year for 3 years.
tension_points.bear_case: Shares were flat after hours because expectations and valuation were already high, and the desk names higher capex and eventual scrutiny of AI customer returns as the main risks.

tension_points.bull_case: Agents expand the overall market and give Shopify, Toast and Square an extra sales channel, while Amazon and Airbnb defend differentiated inventory and direct relationships.
tension_points.bear_case: Agents that control discovery could take a meaningful share of today's advertising and commission pools away from marketplaces.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If agents generate insufficient incremental demand and simply reroute existing orders, the profit pools would migrate to the agents.

tension_points.bull_case: Google claims strong coding performance for Argon, a larger flagship model meant to strengthen its position against Anthropic and OpenAI.
tension_points.bear_case: Some reported benchmarks and employee feedback look less convincing, and limited hands-on access leaves real-world quality unclear.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The key test is how Argon performs once developers begin using it in practice.
